title: Infra/FinOps/Security Monthly Handshake
topics: Q4 budget reconciliation for infra spend
Dedicated vs shared capacity tagging for billing
On-prem testing window for Private deployment
summary: Cross-functional sync to align on SOC2 artifact ownership, finalize infra cost reclassifications for Q4, confirm timeline for VPN cert rotation and a small on-prem validation window. Action owners assigned for artifacts and billing tag cleanup.
next_steps: Omar to circulate SOC2 artifact checklist and current gaps (by 2026-11-09)
Priya to push proposed reclassification spreadsheet and map to cost centers (by 2026-11-12)
Grace/Tom to schedule a 3-hour on-prem validation window for Private deployment (target week of 2026-11-22)
Marcus to prepare a short note on tagging enforcement and automation options (by 2026-11-10)
action_items: Omar Ruiz - Share SOC2 artifact checklist and doc links - due 2026-11-09
Priya Nair - Update Q4 infra reclass spreadsheet and circulate - due 2026-11-12
Grace Kim - Book on-prem validation window and provide runbook - due 2026-11-17
Tom Baker - Rotate VPN certs in staging then production, coordinate downtime - due 2026-11-19
Marcus Chen - Deliver tagging enforcement proposal (scripts + owner mapping) - due 2026-11-10
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-05 14:00 UTC | Duration: 48 mins | Attendees: Lena, Marcus, Grace, Omar, Tom, Priya, Ellen, Samir

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Okay everybody, let's get started. Thanks for joining the monthly infra-finops-compliance handshake. I know calendars are full so we'll try to be crisp.
[00:16] Marcus Chen: Hey, quick mic check — can you all hear me?
[00:19] Samir Patel: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:23] Ellen Park: Good afternoon.
[00:27] Lena Ortiz: Great. First item: SOC 2 artifacts. Omar, you had a pass at the checklist?
[00:33] Omar Ruiz: Yeah I put together a sheet, it's in the drive — soc2-artifact-v2.pdf and a short gap list. I'll share after the call. There's a handful of missing logs from our legacy buildkite runners and some SSO audit exports that need retention confirmation.
[00:47] Priya Nair: When you say "retention confirmation" you mean legal wants 7 years? Or current policy is 3? I thought the policy changed.
[00:56] Omar Ruiz: Sorry, I mean we need to confirm retention period per artifact. Some artifacts are on the 3-year policy, but the legal team flagged a subset that may require extended retention for certain customers. I'll flag them in the doc.
[01:08] Lena Ortiz: Cool. Action: Omar to list which artifacts need extended retention.
[01:12] Omar Ruiz: Yep.
[01:14] [01:20] Marcus Chen: On infra cost side, Priya, we looked at the raw billing and a bunch of untagged GPU pools are landing under "platform-other" which bloats infra spend for product cost centers. We can enforce tagging but need buy-in on renaming the cost centers.
[01:33] Priya Nair: We've got an ask from finance to reclass Q4 so revenue-linked projects aren't absorbing infra noise. I'll prep a reclass spreadsheet.
[01:41] Grace Kim: One thing we noticed, the dedicated pools used for experiments are sometimes not labeled as "dedicated:trial" so autoclaimers don't apply. That leads to unexpected spikes.
[01:52] Samir Patel: There's also the continuous-batching job that got stuck and kept spinning GPUs last week, that wasn't captured by our alert because it reported as a normal pod restart. We'll add a metric for sustained GPU usage.
[02:06] Tom Baker: On the cert rotation — we have a staging cert rotation plan ready, but one question: do we want a rolling restart across regions or a single maintenance window? Rolling minimizes downtime but complicates tracing.
[02:19] Ellen Park: For compliance alignment I'd prefer a single documented window per region, so we can sign off on continuity documents.
[02:27] Marcus Chen: Single window per region sounds fine. We'll script the roll forward.
[02:31] [02:40] Lena Ortiz: Okay, let's go rapid-fire through the checklist: artifacts, tagging, on-prem testing, VPN certs. Omar, list out artifacts and indicate owners. Marcus, tagging proposal. Grace/Tom, book the on-prem test. Priya, reclass spreadsheet.
[02:52] Omar Ruiz: I'm concerned about the buildkite runner logs — they live in a legacy bucket with mixed retention, and the export pipeline only keeps the last 90 days unless we flip a flag. There's a risk if we flip the flag it will increase storage costs.
[03:08] Priya Nair: Right, which is why we need to quantify the incremental cost before changing retention. If it's $2k/month it's different than $20k.
[03:16] Omar Ruiz: Agreed. I'll give a rough estimate in the checklist.
[03:20] Marcus Chen: A note on costs — we might be able to move older logs to a colder tier and have a lifecycle rule. That would keep the retention but reduce monthly spend.
[03:31] Grace Kim: Lifecycle rules are fine, just need to ensure log search for compliance won't break. We can copy indexes to the warm cluster before tiering.
[03:39] [03:50] Samir Patel: For the on-prem test, we only need about 3 hours of runway with one of the M40-equivalent nodes; it's a smoke validation for our Private package. We shouldn't run full load, just functional KV cache and model spin up.
[04:02] Marcus Chen: Yes, and let's ensure the AMI is the same as prod except network ACLs.
[04:08] Tom Baker: I'll schedule a 3-hour window and make notes for rollback — target week of Nov 22.
[04:15] [04:30] Ellen Park: A quick compliance question: do we have clear owners for access reviews? I still see a couple of shadow accounts in the org.
[04:38] Omar Ruiz: We're running an org-wide SSO audit next week. I'll produce the mapping and highlight shadow accounts. That's part of the SOC2 artifact list.
[04:46] Priya Nair: Great. If shadow accounts map to cost centers we need to decide whether to disable or reassign.
[04:52] Lena Ortiz: Let's tie that to the tagging cleanup. Marcus, can your team help identify owner of mysterious service accounts?
[04:58] Marcus Chen: Yes, we'll run a query against last-used and owner-email and attach a ticket.
[05:04] [05:30] (small cross-talk)
[05:36] Lena Ortiz: Any blockers on procurement or vendor agreements that affect SOC2 artifacts?
[05:42] Ellen Park: There's one vendor contract where the vendor provides log retention and we don't have a clean copy of the SLAs in our repo. I'm asking vendor-ops to send a signed copy.
[05:52] Omar Ruiz: Also note, CloudVendorX had a partial outage in EMEA last month and some of our ingest buffers overflowed; there are gaps we need to document for the SOC2 "availability" narrative.
[06:05] Priya Nair: We'll treat that as a customer-impact event and include the post-mortem. Good catch.
[06:12] [06:30] Marcus Chen: Back to infra costs: we should explore automated enforcement — either a webhook on resource creation that checks tags or a nightly job that quarantines untagged resources and notifies owners. Which option is lower touch?
[06:44] Grace Kim: Nightly quarantine is lower risk and easier to roll back; webhook enforcement is better long-term but needs org-wide changes and tests.
[06:52] Marcus Chen: I'll draft both options in one-pager.
[06:56] [07:10] Samir Patel: Question for Omar: when you say SSO audit exports need retention, are we talking raw SAML traces or only token logs? Because token logs are smaller and easier to store.
[07:21] Omar Ruiz: Mostly token logs, some raw traces for failed auth attempts. I'll categorize in the sheet.
[07:28] [07:40] Tom Baker: Cert rotation — I've got a staging runbook but need agreement on maintenance notification cadence. How much lead time does compliance expect?
[07:50] Ellen Park: Two weeks for major cert changes, seven days for minor. All communicated via the change log and the continuity register.
[07:58] Tom Baker: Noted.
[08:05] [08:20] (background keyboard)
[08:25] Lena Ortiz: Anything else on the SOC2 side?
[08:28] Omar Ruiz: Also need to check our HSM access logs — some KMS rotations didn't log properly because of a missing agent. That's another line item.
[08:36] Priya Nair: If HSM access logs are incomplete we need to escalate to Legal. How incomplete?
[08:42] Omar Ruiz: About two weeks worth around the time we did the key import; agent crashed and never restarted.
[08:48] Marcus Chen: We can try replaying the syslog collector; if not possible we'll include the incident in the SOC2 narrative.
[08:55] [09:10] (laughter)
[09:16] Grace Kim: On the on-prem validation, can we do a quick dependency map? I'm worried network ACLs will block an external metrics push.
[09:25] Samir Patel: We'll open an ingress for the metrics cluster during the test and close after. Minimal blast radius.
[09:31] Grace Kim: Perfect.
[09:36] [09:50] Lena Ortiz: Okay, let's capture the decisions: 1) Omar will enumerate artifacts and retention needs with cost estimate; 2) Priya will propose reclass; 3) Marcus will propose tagging enforcement options; 4) Tom/Grace to schedule on-prem validation; 5) Omar to run SSO and HSM access audits. Anything to add?
[10:06] Priya Nair: I'll also flag any contracts that could change retention obligations.
[10:10] Ellen Park: I'll follow up on the vendor SLA copy.
[10:14] Omar Ruiz: I'll include the buildkite runner lifecycle cost estimate.
[10:18] [10:30] (pause)
[10:36] Marcus Chen: One more small ask — a weekend maintenance window for a tagging enforcement rollout might be easiest. We should aim for one weekend in early December.
[10:47] Priya Nair: Finance prefers weekdays for cost reporting, but we'll make an exception for infra maintenance if it reduces misbilling.
[10:55] Lena Ortiz: Put a placeholder: weekend of Dec 5. Marcus, don't lock it until Priya thumbs up.
[11:03] [11:20] Tom Baker: I'll coordinate with SRE on runbooks and on-call rotation for that weekend.
[11:26] (brief silence)
[11:35] Lena Ortiz: Alright final round — any blockers on timeline?
[11:40] Samir Patel: No blockers, just need clarity on the test AMI.
[11:45] Grace Kim: We'll publish the AMI ID in the ticket.
[11:49] Omar Ruiz: Nothing else from security, will send the checklist.
[11:53] Priya Nair: I'll send the spreadsheet draft today EOD.
[11:57] Lena Ortiz: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene if any critical blockers pop up.
[12:03] (meeting ends)

Notes/Links mentioned: soc2-artifact-v2.pdf (drive link), Q4-reclass-spreadsheet.xlsx (drive link), on-prem-validation-runbook.md (internal wiki), tagging-enforcement-proposal-draft.md

Transcription notes: occasional overlapping speech, a few proper nouns mistranscribed (Buildkite sometimes came out as "build kit"), timestamps approximate every 30-90 seconds.
